title: EA Cancels Return of College Basketball Video Game
summary: Win money playing your favorite video games
body_text: 2K Takes over College Basketball Return After the smashing success of College Football 25, who’s first trailer doubled the views of the first Madden 25 trailer last year, with over 28 million views on X within the first 48 hours of its release, EA Sports was trying to recapture that magic with a different sport. EA Sports had announced the return of their College Basketball video game series early this year, however those plans were scrapped when some colleges refused to go with EA and chose to go with a 2K College Basketball videogame instead. It remains to be seen what 2Ks plans will be, but the success that EA had with College Football 25 and 26, will not continue with College Basketball. EA Sports success with College Football was a major reason for this decision. Was an expected 2028 Release While the initial announcement was met with much fanfare and anticipation it was still going to be awhile before EA was planning on releasing another College Basketball game. 2028 was the expected release date that was mentioned by EA Sports. If 2K goes into the College Basketball world, it is reasonable to think that it wouldn’t take them as long due to the game engine they currently have already with NBA2K. The biggest hurdle that 2K would have, may be getting every D1 College to sign on for the videogame, which was what caused EA to scrape the idea all together. First College Basketball Game since NCAA Basketball 10 The possibility of an upcoming release of a college basketball video game by a major company, has such hype around it due to how long it’s been since the last release of one. You have to go all the way back to 2009 with the release of NCAA Basketball 10, for the last college basketball video game. With Blake Griffin on the cover in his Oklahoma jersey, NCAA Basketball 10 released in 2009 on the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3. The return of a College Basketball franchise would be a shot of nostalgia to college basketball fans and gamers around the world, who grew up playing college basketball video games on their Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3. title: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge prior authorization form pdf filler
summary: A clinician's walkthrough of the CMS form and a tool to generate a PDF.
body_text: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge prior authorization form pdf filler Brandon Ballinger · Jul 1, 2026 Medicare covers GLP-1s for $50/month starting July 1, but requires prior authorization. The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge prior authorization form is a PDF with one page of contact fields and twelve yes/no questions that determine patient eligibility based on their BMI, medical history, and eligibility for GLP-1s through Part D. Medicare GLP-1 bridge prior auth form filler You can download the PDF of Medicare’s GLP-1 prior auth form here. You can also use the below generator to fill in the MedicareGLP-1 prior auth PDF so that it’s ready to fax or send electronically: You can also just use the direct link to the Medicare GLP-1 Prior auth PDF generator . For the policy background (who’s eligible, what the Bridge costs, and how it sunsets at the end of 2027), see Medicare covers GLP-1s for $50/month . Patient eligibility for GLP-1 Bridge prior auths About 4 million Medicare beneficiaries are likely to be eligible for GLP-1 bridge. To be eligible for a prior auth, patients need to: 1. have a BMI >=35 or >= 27 with other qualifying chronic conditions, 2. Not have GLP-1 coverage through Part D, 3. have a denied pharmacy claim. We’ll cover each of these. A denied claim has to come before the prior auth Before you submit the prior authorization, the pharmacy has to transmit a claim to the GLP-1 Bridge billing channel and have it denied. The pharmacy should use the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge BIN (028918) and PCN (MEDDGLP1BR). Have the pharmacy run the claim first, then file. Step 2: complete the GLP-1 Bridge prior auth form The top of the form is standard contact information: patient name, Medicare Beneficiary Identifier (MBI), date of birth, and address, plus your name, NPI, tax ID, and practice contact details. Then you select one requested drug and answer twelve questions. The first four questions are a filter. The Bridge only covers GLP-1s prescribed purely for weight loss. If the patient has a Part D-eligible diagnosis, the request belongs with their Part D plan instead, not the Bridge: Q Question If yes Q1 Acknowledge that Part D-eligible diagnoses route to the Part D plan Acknowledge to continue Q2 Moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea? Submit to Part D plan Q3 Noncirrhotic MASH with moderate-to-advanced fibrosis? Submit to Part D plan Q4 Type 2 diabetes? Submit to Part D plan If none of those apply, you continue to the weight-management questions: Q Question Q5 Patient is 18+, using the drug for weight reduction and maintenance alongside lifestyle modification, and which BMI range applies at GLP-1 initiation Q6 Pre-diabetes (ADA criteria)? Q7 Previous myocardial infarction? Q8 Previous stroke? Q9 Symptomatic peripheral artery disease? Q10 Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction? Q11 Uncontrolled hypertension (>140 systolic or >90 diastolic despite two antihypertensives)? Q12 Chronic kidney disease stage 3a or above? Q5 is worth some explanation. Medicare GLP-1 coverage is based on BMI at the time the patient initiated GLP-1 therapy . It notes explicitly that if BMI has dropped since starting, you select the initial range. For example, a patient who started at a BMI of 37 and is now at 32 is recorded as the higher range. In other words, your patients using GLP-1s for maintenance are likely eligible Medicare’s Bridge program. Patient eligibility requirements for GLP-1 bridge The specific eligibility requirements for Medicare Bridge depend on the patient’s BMI, with different requirements at 35+, 30-25, and 27-30. This table shows the exact requirements by BMI; the prior auth will be denied if they don’t meet these requirements: Patient BMI What else they need 35 or higher Nothing else required 30 or higher Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or chronic kidney disease (stage 3a or higher) 27 or higher Pre-diabetes, a prior heart attack, a prior stroke, or symptomatic peripheral artery disease Step 3: submit the prior auth PDF via CoverMyMeds or fax Once the form is complete and a denied claim is on file, submit it one of two ways: an electronic prior authorization through CoverMyMeds, or by fax to the number printed on the form. Which specific GLP-1 drugs Medicare Bridge covers Medicare Bridge covers Foundayo (orforglipron) tablets, Wegovy (semaglutide) injection, HD injection, and tablets, and Zepbound (tirzepatide) KwikPen. The single-dose vial and single-dose pen formulations of Zepbound are not covered by Medicare Bridge. Things that delay a Bridge prior authorization Most holdups trace back to the same handful of issues: submitting the prior authorization before a denied claim is on file (the pharmacy must first run and have the claim denied to BIN 028918 / PCN MEDDGLP1BR); listing the patient’s current BMI on Q5 instead of their BMI at initiation, which may mistakenly disqualify them if their BMI has improved; routing a Part D-eligible diagnosis such as sleep apnea, MASH, type 2 diabetes, or established cardiovascular disease to the Bridge instead of the Part D plan; or leaving any form fields incomplete, since submissions are limited to clinicians and partial forms will be rejected. This post is part of our series on Medicare coverage for cardiovascular health . See also: Medicare covers GLP-1s for $50/month and how patients enroll in the GLP-1 Bridge . title: En la Clínica de las Américas, Zebra Technologies revoluciona la atención con una mejora del 40% en la precisión del servicio
summary: La institución mejoró las tasas de satisfacción en la atención de pacientes gracias a la tecnología.
body_text: La institución mejoró las tasas de satisfacción en la atención de pacientes gracias a la tecnología SANTA CRUZ DE LA SIERRA, Bolivia – Sep. 12, 2024 - Zebra Technologies Corporation (NASDAQ: ZBRA) líder mundial en soluciones digitales para la gestión de activos, información y personas, celebra la exitosa implementación de sus tecnologías en la Clínica de las Américas, uno de los centros de salud más emblemáticos de Santa Cruz. La clínica ha conseguido mejorar la exactitud de la atención al paciente hasta un 40%, tras la puesta en marcha de una solución, la cual ha mejorado la calidad del servicio sanitario, así como su eficacia. La Clínica de las Américas, que diariamente ve a más de 300 pacientes, ha incorporado soluciones innovadoras de Zebra como el escáner DS2208-HC , las impresoras ZD510-HC y ZD421 , o las impresoras de tarjetas ZC300 , que han permitido una mejor coordinación entre el personal médico y no médico, una mejor supervisión del recorrido del paciente y una mejor precisión de la gestión de procesos; lo cual nos ha resultado en una atención más eficiente y de mayor calidad. El Dr. Felipe Teles, Director Médico Ejecutivo de la Clínica de las Américas subraya que "la integración de las soluciones de Zebra representó una mejora significativa en esta clínica. La eficacia de estas herramientas en la mejora de nuestra calidad de atención se traduce en el incremento del 40% de la precisión del servicio. Nos sentimos satisfechos con la creación de un tratamiento personalizado, con la mejora de la comunicación y de la gestión del inventario." Por otro lado, la satisfacción de los pacientes ha aumentado considerablemente; el 80% están conformes con la evolución del triaje y el 91 % con la asistencia médica en general. La cooperación con el socio estratégico de Zebra, Hiller S.A., ha sido esencial para alcanzar estos avances. Oscar Pedraza, Gerente División Sistemas de Hiller S.A., indica "La transformación digital es clave para optimizar la visibilidad y la seguridad en los servicios de salud". Zebra presenta soluciones a medida que van acorde con estas necesidades y aseguran una atención de primer nivel. Zebra ofrece una gama completa de soluciones diseñadas específicamente para el sector de la salud, utilizando impresoras de pulseras y etiquetas, escáneres de códigos de barras, computadoras móviles, tablets, software de comunicación y sistemas de localización en tiempo real (RTLS) para facilitar una mejor colaboración en la atención, mejorar la comunicación y optimizar la eficiencia de los flujos de trabajo a lo largo de la jornada del paciente,” señaló Alejandro Prosperi, Vicepresidente de Ventas y Gerente General para el Sur de América Latina en Zebra Technologies. “Empoderamos a los equipos de salud para resolver problemas de manera eficiente, permitiendo que los profesionales de la salud recuperen su tiempo y dediquen más tiempo al cuidado de los pacientes.” ### ACERCA DE ZEBRA Zebra (NASDAQ: ZBRA) ayuda a las organizaciones a monitorizar, anticiparse y acelerar sus flujos de trabajo potenciando su primera línea y garantizando que todo y todos sean visibles, estén conectados y totalmente optimizados. Nuestro galardonado porfolio abarca desde software hasta innovaciones en robótica, visión artificial, automatización y toma de decisiones digital, todo ello respaldado por un legado de más de 50 años en soluciones de escaneado, seguimiento y localización e informática móvil. Con un ecosistema de 10.000 socios en más de 100 países, Zebra cuenta entre sus clientes a más del 80% de las empresas Fortune 500. Newsweek ha reconocido a Zebra recientemente como uno de los lugares de trabajo más queridos de Estados Unidos, así como una de las mejores empresas para la diversidad, y estamos en la lista Fast Company’s de los mejores lugares de trabajo para innovadores.
